function_question: How does nature grip on wet, slippery surfaces?

opening.text: There was a girl called Mina who visited her Grandma every weekend.
Grandma stepped out of her front door to water her roses and chat to the birds in her garden.
It rained, and Grandma's foot slid on the wet doorstep. She grabbed the door just in time. "That step is like ice when it's wet," she sighed.

card.problem: Grandma slips on the wet step
card.goal: A sole or mat that grips on a wet slope
card.rules: Test on a wet ramp, never on a real step

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: A slip in the rain
chapters.line: Mina wonders: why is a wet step so slippery, and how can we stop it?

chapters.title: Mina needs a partner
chapters.line: Grandma needs two clever inventors. Will you join Mina?

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Mina's Grandma slips on her doorstep every time it rains. Can you help Mina design a sole or mat that grips, even when it's wet? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some inventors already have a spark of an idea for stopping slips. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature has been gripping wet surfaces for millions of years. Tap each card to meet four heroes who never slip!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Which material will grip the wet ramp at the steepest angle?
guide.sketch: Time to draw your sole from underneath, with arrows showing where the water goes!
guide.build_and_test: Build your sample, spray the ramp and lift it slowly. How steep can it go before your sample slides?
guide.retry_tip: Inventors never stop at round 1. Change ONE thing, like deeper channels, and test again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, Grandma's doorstep has YOUR frog-foot mat, and she walks out to her roses rain or shine.

quick_check.question: A smooth plastic sole slides on the wet ramp at 15°. Mina's frog-pad sole holds on until 35°. How many degrees steeper is that?
quick_check.right: Right! 35 − 15 = 20. Mina's sole grips a much steeper wet ramp.
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Take the smaller angle away from the bigger one.

clue_cards.name: Tree frog
clue_cards.trick: Its toe pads have tiny tiles with channels between them.
clue_cards.does: The channels drain water away, so the pad grips wet leaves.

clue_cards.name: Gecko
clue_cards.trick: Its toes have millions of tiny hairs.
clue_cards.does: The hairs touch every little bump, so it can walk up glass.

clue_cards.name: Octopus
clue_cards.trick: It has hundreds of suckers on its arms.
clue_cards.does: Each sucker seals against wet rock and holds tight in the waves.

clue_cards.name: Cat
clue_cards.trick: It has soft, squishy paw pads.
clue_cards.does: The pads squash into tiny bumps and grip when it lands.

match_groups.label: 🧸 Soft or hairy, touches every bump

items.label: Smooth plastic on a wet slope
A soft rubber boot sole with deep grooves on a wet slope

predict.explain: A thin layer of water acts like a slide between two smooth surfaces. Grooves give the water somewhere to go, so soft rubber can touch the ground and grip.

lab.title: The slide-or-stick lab
lab.predict: Tape each material under a box on a wet ramp. Which will grip at the steepest angle?

tool.name: 5 Whys
tool.intro: You already know how to ask 5 whys. Today you're a root detective: keep asking why until you find the real reason people slip.

parts.name: Why #1
parts.example: 🪴 Why is it wilting? It's thirsty.

parts.name: Why #2
parts.example: 🪴 Why is it thirsty? The soil dries out fast.
parts.starter: Why does her shoe slide on the step? Because…

parts.name: Why #3
parts.example: 🪴 Why does it dry fast? The pot is in hot sun all day.
parts.starter: Why is there water between her shoe and the step? Because…

parts.name: Why #4
parts.example: 🪴 Why? It sits on the sunny windowsill.
parts.starter: Why doesn't the water run away? Because…

parts.name: Why #5
parts.what: Find the root cause, then fix that.
parts.example: 🪴 Why? Nobody knew it likes shade. Fix: move it!
parts.starter: Why can't the sole touch the step? Because…
